entries.content_plain: 7. sound wisdom-- literally, "substance," opposed to what is fictitious. According to the context, this may be assistance, as here corresponding with buckler-- or safety, or wisdom, which procures it (compare Pr 3:21 ; 8:14 ; 18:1 ; Job 6:13 ; 12:13 ). layeth up-- provides, ever ready.
entries.reader_content_plain: 7. sound wisdom-- literally, "substance," opposed to what is fictitious. According to the context, this may be assistance, as here corresponding with buckler-- or safety, or wisdom, which procures it (compare Pr 3:21 ; 8:14 ; 18:1 ; Job 6:13 ; 12:13 ). layeth up-- provides, ever ready.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7206"/><div sID="gen11108" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7206"/>16-19. Deliverance from another danger.<div eID="gen11108" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen11109" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the strange woman--</hi>This term is often used for harlot, or loose woman (<reference osisRef="Judg.11.1">Jud 11:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.11.2">2</reference>), married (<reference osisRef="Prov.7.5">Pr 7:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Prov.7.19">19</reference>) or not (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.11.1">1Ki 11:1</reference>), so called, because such were, perhaps at first, foreigners, though "strange" may also denote whatever is opposed to right or proper, as "strange fire" (<reference osisRef="Num.3.4">Nu 3:4</reference>); "strange incense" (<reference osisRef="Exod.30.9">Ex 30:9</reference>).<div eID="gen11109" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen11110" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">flattereth--</hi>literally, "smooths."<div eID="gen11110" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen11111" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">her words--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.5.9">Psa 5:9</reference>). <div eID="gen11111" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 16-19. Deliverance from another danger. the strange woman-- This term is often used for harlot, or loose woman ( Jud 11:1 , 2 ), married ( Pr 7:5 , 19 ) or not ( 1Ki 11:1 ), so called, because such were, perhaps at first, foreigners, though "strange" may also denote whatever is opposed to right or proper, as "strange fire" ( Nu 3:4 ); "strange incense" ( Ex 30:9 ). flattereth-- literally, "smooths." her words-- ( Psa 5:9 ).
entries.reader_content_plain: 16-19. Deliverance from another danger. the strange woman-- This term is often used for harlot, or loose woman ( Jud 11:1 , 2 ), married ( Pr 7:5 , 19 ) or not ( 1Ki 11:1 ), so called, because such were, perhaps at first, foreigners, though "strange" may also denote whatever is opposed to right or proper, as "strange fire" ( Nu 3:4 ); "strange incense" ( Ex 30:9 ). flattereth-- literally, "smooths." her words-- ( Psa 5:9 ).
